q: You raid a brick kiln and rescue a 15-year-old girl sent by contractor who says she agreed to work off family debt. Action?
options: Return her on consent letter
Treat as trafficking/bonded labour; consent irrelevant, register FIR, rescue, rehab and child welfare referral
Fine parents only
Let kiln hold her till debt paid
expl: Traffic, begar and bonded debt are banned; child's consent no defence.
why: Exploitation law voids consent under coercion. Immediate rescue plus welfare link breaks debt trap and secures evidence.
trapnote: Trap: validates consent to bonded labour.

q: A cracker unit in Guntur employs a 12-year-old; owner says after school hours so legal. Nearby dhaba employs 16-year-old at stove. Your finding?
options: Both legal as part-time
Under-14 barred in all work; 14-18 barred in hazardous work, so book kiln owner and regulate dhaba with safeguards
Only fine parents
Seal school instead
expl: Under 14 ban is total; adolescents barred in hazardous processes.
why: Age-tier ban targets physical risk. SI must rescue younger child and prosecute employer, not normalise after-school labour.
trapnote: Trap: part-time equals lawful for child.

q: Dalit devotees are stopped at village temple gate by custom claim. Priest cites a famous hill-shrine case as settled bar on entry. Your duty?
options: Uphold custom and disperse devotees
Enforce temple entry and register untouchability/PoA case; hill-shrine review is pending, not settled law to deny entry
Ask devotees to build separate temple
Refer to panchayat vote
expl: Temple-entry ban on caste grounds is punishable; PoA FIR mandatory.
why: Custom cannot trump equality and entry statutes. Pending larger-bench review means no final bar can be cited.
trapnote: Trap: cites pending shrine reference as settled.

q: A wholly state-funded school starts compulsory scripture classes; nearby aided minority school seeks to manage staff per its rules. Advise?
options: Both can impose religious instruction freely
State-funded school cannot impart religious instruction; aided minority school keeps administration subject to reasonable regulation
Close both schools
Police fixes syllabus
expl: Wholly-funded institutions bar religious instruction; aided minority bodies face regulation that cannot destroy minority character.
why: Funding test separates the two regimes. SI prevents breach of peace without dictating curriculum or appointments.
trapnote: Trap: applies same rule to funded vs aided.

q: A Telugu trust founded by non-minority businessmen, now staffed only by minority teachers, claims minority-school autonomy to defy fee audit. Check?
options: Grant status on current staff pattern
Minority protection needs both establishment and administration by minority; otherwise no 30(1) shield, audit continues
Exempt all private schools from audit
SI grants minority certificate
expl: Establish plus administer by minority is twin test.
why: Origin and control decide character, not present workforce. SI holds order while education dept verifies founding deed.
